issues.description: The struct property 'name' of Genre is declared with private visibility in the solution implementation but is expected to be readable and is accessed elsewhere. Problem statement (problem_statement.md lines 19-20) defines Genre as having a String 'name' and optional 'subgenre'. In Sources/BookstoreLib/Bookstore.swift (solution) the property is declared 'private let name: String' (line 42), while Sources/BookstoreLib/Client.swift (solution) reads 'genre.name' (line 19). This visibility mismatch prevents the Client code from compiling and contradicts the problem's expectation that Genre.name is publicly readable for printing, which will block students from running the example output and from using the field as described.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Genre.name property non-private so it can be read by the Client and match the problem description. For example, change 'private let name: String' to 'let name: String' (internal visibility) or to 'public let name: String' if explicit cross-module access is required.
